name: azure_key_vault
description: Manages an Azure Key Vault — a managed store for secrets, keys and certificates, provisioned within an environment and resource group. Platform-provisioned vaults always use Azure RBAC: the resource group's managed identity is granted Key Vault Administrator at resource-group scope, so workloads bound to that group can read secrets with no per-vault permission setup.

attributes.name: workspace_id
attributes.description: Workspace that owns this vault (path parameter).

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Vault name. 3–24 characters, letters, numbers and hyphens only; must start with a letter, end with a letter or number, and contain no consecutive hyphens. Must be globally unique within Azure — note that a soft-deleted vault keeps its name reserved until it is purged.

attributes.name: environment_id
attributes.description: Environment the vault is provisioned into.

attributes.name: resource_group_id
attributes.description: Resource group the vault is provisioned into. Its managed identity is what gets Key Vault Administrator on the vault.

attributes.name: scope_ids
attributes.description: Scopes the vault is visible to. Inherited from the resource group.

attributes.name: sku_name
attributes.description: Pricing tier. Standard is sufficient for secrets and certificates; Premium adds HSM-backed keys.

attributes.name: soft_delete_retention_days
attributes.description: How long a deleted vault or secret stays recoverable before Azure permanently removes it. Soft delete itself cannot be disabled.

attributes.name: enable_purge_protection
attributes.description: Prevent permanent deletion during the retention period. One-way in Azure: it can be turned on, but turning it off is rejected - the vault has to be recreated. Setting it back to false is refused at plan time rather than failing mid-apply; use lifecycle { ignore_changes = [enable_purge_protection] } if you want Terraform to leave an already-protected vault alone. It also blocks purging a soft-deleted vault, so after a destroy the name stays reserved for the full soft_delete_retention_days and cannot be reused before then.

attributes.name: purge_on_deprovision
attributes.description: Deprecated and ignored. Azure keeps a deleted vault soft-deleted for soft_delete_retention_days, and its globally-unique name stays reserved for that period. To create a new vault with the same name, purge the soft-deleted one in Azure first (az keyvault purge --name <name>) - which is only possible when enable_purge_protection is false.
attributes.deprecated: No longer used. The platform does not purge the vault on deprovision; to reuse a vault's name, purge the soft-deleted vault in Azure first.

attributes.name: enabled_for_deployment
attributes.description: Allow Azure Virtual Machines to retrieve certificates stored as secrets. Kubernetes workloads do not need this — they use the Secrets Store CSI driver with workload identity.

attributes.name: enabled_for_disk_encryption
attributes.description: Allow Azure Disk Encryption to retrieve secrets and unwrap keys.

attributes.name: enabled_for_template_deployment
attributes.description: Allow ARM template deployments to retrieve secrets during deployment.

attributes.name: network_acls
attributes.description: Network rules controlling who can reach the vault's data plane.

attributes.name: public_network_access
attributes.description: Enabled makes the vault reachable over its public endpoint, subject to default_action. Disabled allows private endpoints only.

attributes.name: default_action
attributes.description: What to do with traffic that matches no rule. Allow accepts any network; Deny accepts only the addresses in ip_rules and the subnets in vnet_rules.

attributes.name: ip_rules
attributes.description: IPv4 addresses or CIDR ranges allowed through when default_action is Deny.

attributes.name: vnet_rules
attributes.description: ARM resource ids of subnets allowed through when default_action is Deny.

attributes.name: bypass_azure_services
attributes.description: Let trusted Microsoft services bypass the firewall.

attributes.name: tags
attributes.description: Azure resource tags. Platform-managed duplocloud-ai-* tags are added automatically and are not tracked here.

attributes.name: provisioner_type
attributes.description: How the platform provisions the vault. Defaults to the environment's provisioner.

attributes.name: provisioner_version
attributes.description: Provisioner version. Defaults to the environment's version.

attributes.name: enable_rbac_authorization
attributes.description: Whether the vault's data plane uses Azure RBAC. Always true for platform-provisioned vaults, and immutable — flipping it would silently change who can read every secret, so the platform requires a recreate instead.

attributes.name: azure_resource_group_name
attributes.description: Name of the Azure resource group the vault lives in.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Provisioning status reported by the platform.

attributes.name: vault_record_id
attributes.description: Backend identifier of the vault record.

attributes.name: key_vault_id
attributes.description: ARM resource id of the Key Vault in Azure.

attributes.name: vault_uri
attributes.description: Data-plane URI clients use to read secrets, e.g. https://my-app-vault.vault.azure.net/.

attributes.name: provisioning_state
attributes.description: Azure-reported provisioning state of the vault.

attributes.name: tenant_id
attributes.description: Microsoft Entra tenant that backs the vault's authentication.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.description: Timestamp when the vault record was created (RFC 3339, normalized to UTC at second precision).

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.description: Timestamp when the vault record was last updated (RFC 3339, normalized to UTC at second precision).

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Version counter, incremented on each update.
